Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Provided are a reference scale and dimension measurement system that make it possible to maintain accurate measurement even if the reference scale is not disposed or projected on a measurement surface. A dimension measurement device according to the present invention is provided with: a reference scale extraction means for extracting, from photographed image data including a reference scale that includes a film that has a pattern for displaying a length reference formed on the surface thereof and a lens that is in contact with the film, an image in which an image of the length reference is formed on the basis of the relationship between a pattern function expressing the length reference projected onto the lens according to variation in a prescribed angle between the reference scale and the optical axis of a photography device and an image formation color function indicating the image of the length reference formed on the imaging device; an object of measurement extraction means for extracting an object of measurement image from photographed image data including the reference scale; and a dimension calculation means for calculating a dimension of the object of measurement on the basis of a dimension of the image in which the image of the length reference is formed and the image of the object of measurement.

outputs.L1: Provided are a reference scale and a dimension measurement system capable of maintaining measurement accuracy even when the reference scale is neither disposed on nor projected onto a measurement surface. A dimension measurement device according to the present invention includes: reference scale extraction means for extracting, from photographed image data containing a reference scale comprising a film having a pattern formed on its surface to indicate a length reference and a lens in contact with the film, an image in which the length reference is formed, based on the relationship between a pattern function representing the length reference projected onto the lens in accordance with variations in a prescribed angle between the reference scale and the optical axis of a photography device, and an image-formation color function indicating the image of the length reference formed on an imaging device; object-of-measurement extraction means for extracting an image of an object of measurement from photographed image data containing the reference scale; and dimension calculation means for calculating a dimension of the object of measurement based on a dimension of the image in which the length reference is formed and the image of the object of measurement.
outputs.L2: Disclosed are a reference scale and a dimensional measurement system capable of preserving measurement accuracy even when the reference scale is neither placed on nor projected onto the surface being measured. The dimensional measurement device includes a reference-scale extraction unit, a measurement-target extraction unit, and a dimension calculation unit. The reference-scale extraction unit processes captured image data containing a reference scale composed of a film, whose surface carries a pattern representing a length standard, and a lens contacting the film. It extracts an image of the length standard using the correlation between: (i) a pattern function describing how the length-standard pattern is projected onto the lens as a specified angle between the reference scale and the optical axis of an imaging device changes; and (ii) an image-formation color function identifying the length-standard image produced on the imaging device. The measurement-target extraction unit obtains an image of the object to be measured from captured image data that includes the reference scale. The dimension calculation unit then determines the object’s dimension from the dimensions of the formed length-standard image and the extracted measurement-object image.
outputs.L3:
The system is designed to maintain accurate dimensional measurements even when the reference scale is not positioned or projected directly on the surface of the object being measured. The reference scale comprises a patterned film that displays a known length reference and a lens placed in contact with the film.

A reference-scale extraction component processes the photographed image data to identify the image of the length reference. This identification is performed using the angle of the reference scale relative to the camera’s optical axis, together with an image-formation color function associated with the scale. An object extraction component then detects and isolates the measurement object from the same photographed image data containing the reference scale.

Finally, a dimension calculation component compares the extracted image of the measurement object with the extracted length-reference image. Based on this comparison, the component calculates the dimensions of the object, enabling reliable measurement without requiring the reference scale to be located directly on the measurement surface.
outputs.L4:
A reference-scale and dimension-measurement system determines the size of a target object from photographed image data. The image includes both the target object and a length-reference image projected through a lens. An image-processing unit extracts the projected reference image and the target object from the photograph and identifies their relevant edges, feature points, or measurement regions.

Because the reference scale may be inclined relative to the optical axis of the camera, its apparent length in the photograph can differ from its actual reference length. The system therefore determines or obtains information indicating the angle between the scale and the camera’s optical axis. Using this angle, along with the detected size and position of the projected reference image, the system corrects for perspective, inclination, and projection-related distortion to establish an appropriate conversion between image coordinates and real-world dimensions.

The corrected reference information is then applied to the extracted image of the target object. Distances between selected points, boundaries, or other features of the object are measured in the image and converted into actual dimensions. The resulting measurements may include the object’s length, width, diameter, spacing, or other dimensional characteristics.

This arrangement eliminates the need to place a physical ruler directly against the object or to project the reference image onto the same surface as the feature being measured. Accurate dimensions can therefore be obtained even when the reference scale is offset from, inclined to, or otherwise not coincident with the measurement surface, improving flexibility and ease of use in locations where direct scale placement is difficult or impractical.
outputs.L5:
**Provided**

The word “provided” often refers to something that has been supplied, offered, or made available. For example, a company may provide employees with the tools they need to work effectively. In this context, “provided” indicates that those resources have already been given.

“Provided” can also introduce a condition, similar to “if” or “as long as.” For instance: “You may attend the event, provided that you register in advance.” Here, attendance is possible only when the stated requirement is met.

Whether used to describe supplied resources or establish a condition, “provided” is a versatile word commonly found in everyday communication, business documents, and formal agreements.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a dimension measurement system that uses a reference scale with a patterned film and contacting lens, allowing accurate measurements even when the scale is not placed directly on the measurement surface.
counterfactuals.output: A dimension measurement system includes a reference scale configured to be positioned relative to an object to be measured, an imaging device, and a processor. The reference scale comprises a film having a predetermined pattern and a contacting lens optically coupled to the film. The contacting lens provides a defined optical relationship between the patterned film, the measurement surface, and the imaging device, thereby reducing measurement error caused by spacing, perspective, parallax, or magnification when the reference scale is not placed directly on the measurement surface. The imaging device captures an image containing the predetermined pattern and at least a portion of the object. The processor detects features of the predetermined pattern, determines a spatial calibration and, based on the calibration, calculates one or more dimensions of the object. The system thus enables accurate non-contact or offset dimension measurement while reducing sensitivity to placement of the reference scale.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for measuring object dimensions from photographed image data by extracting both a length-reference image and the object image, then calculating dimensions from their relative image sizes.
counterfactuals.output:
An image-based dimension-measuring invention uses a photograph containing both a target object and a reference marker of known length. An image processor identifies and extracts the object image and the length-reference image, then determines their respective pixel lengths, widths, areas, or other image-size parameters. A scale factor is calculated by comparing the measured image size of the reference marker with its known physical dimension. The processor applies this scale factor to the corresponding image dimensions of the object to calculate the object’s actual length, width, height, diameter, area, or other dimensions.

The invention may include automatic edge detection, perspective and lens-distortion correction, reference-marker recognition, and an output interface that overlays or displays the calculated dimensions. Accurate results are obtained when the reference and object are photographed under equivalent imaging conditions, preferably in the same plane, or after correcting for differences in perspective or distance.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal technical summary of a dimension measurement device comprising reference scale extraction means, measurement-object extraction means, and dimension calculation means.
counterfactuals.output:
A dimension measurement device is configured to determine one or more dimensions of a measurement object from acquired image data. The device comprises reference scale extraction means, measurement-object extraction means, and dimension calculation means.

The reference scale extraction means detects a reference scale represented in the image data and derives calibration information corresponding to a known physical length. The measurement-object extraction means identifies the measurement object, separates it from the surrounding image region, and extracts geometric features, boundaries, or characteristic points defining the dimension to be measured. The dimension calculation means determines a dimensional value of the measurement object by converting a measured image-space distance between the extracted features into a physical-space distance using the calibration information obtained from the reference scale.

The device may further perform image correction, scale-orientation compensation, perspective correction, noise reduction, and extraction-confidence evaluation to improve measurement accuracy. The resulting dimensional value may be displayed, stored, or transmitted to an external processing or inspection system.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain a camera-based measurement system that compensates for changes in the angle between the camera’s optical axis and a reference scale using a pattern function and an image formation color function.
counterfactuals.output:
A camera-based measurement system can correct angular misalignment by modeling both the known reference-scale pattern and the way that pattern appears in the camera image.

### 1. Reference scale and pattern function

The reference scale carries a known spatial pattern—such as alternating bars, colored regions, coded marks, or a continuously varying color pattern. A **pattern function**

\[
P(s)
\]

describes the scale at physical coordinate \(s\). Its value may indicate intensity, color, or a vector of color-channel values, for example

\[
P(s)=[R(s),G(s),B(s)].
\]

Because the pattern is known in physical coordinates, image features can be associated with positions on the scale.

### 2. Image formation color function

The color recorded by a camera is generally not equal to the nominal pattern color. It also depends on viewing angle, illumination, lens response, sensor spectral response, focus, and possibly the directional optical properties of the scale.

An **image formation color function** models this relationship:

\[
\hat{\mathbf c}(u)
=
F\!\left(P(s(u;\theta)),\,\theta,\,\boldsymbol{\eta}\right),
\]

where:

- \(u\) is an image coordinate,
- \(s(u;\theta)\) maps that image coordinate to a scale coordinate,
- \(\theta\) is the angle between the camera optical axis and the scale’s reference direction or normal,
- \(\boldsymbol{\eta}\) contains other calibrated imaging parameters,
- \(\hat{\mathbf c}(u)\) is the predicted camera color.

The function \(F\) may be obtained from a physical optical model or from calibration images acquired at known angles.

### 3. Estimating the viewing angle

For a captured image, the system compares measured pixel colors \(\mathbf c_{\text{obs}}(u)\) with colors predicted for different candidate angles. It estimates the angle and other pose parameters by minimizing an error such as

\[
(\hat{\theta},\hat{\mathbf p})
=
\arg\min_{\theta,\mathbf p}
\sum_u
\left\|
\mathbf c_{\text{obs}}(u)
-
F\!\left(P(s(u;\theta,\mathbf p)),\theta,\boldsymbol{\eta}\right)
\right\|^2.
\]

Here, \(\mathbf p\) can include scale translation, distance, magnification, rotation, illumination level, or camera gain. A robust loss can be used to reduce the influence of glare, dirt, or occlusion.

### 4. Correcting the measurement

Once \(\hat{\theta}\) is known, the system removes the geometric distortion caused by the oblique view. In a simple one-dimensional case, an apparent image displacement may be corrected by a factor related to \(\cos\hat{\theta}\). In a general system, the estimated angle is used in a projective camera model or homography:

\[
s = H^{-1}(u;\hat{\theta},\hat{\mathbf p}).
\]

The resulting coordinate \(s\) is therefore expressed in the physical coordinate system of the reference scale rather than in distorted image pixels.

### 5. Practical operation

A typical measurement cycle is:

1. Capture an image containing the reference scale and the object or indicator to be measured.
2. Extract the scale region and its pixel-color values.
3. Evaluate the known pattern function at candidate scale positions.
4. Use the image formation color function to predict how the pattern should look at candidate angles.
5. Fit the prediction to the image to estimate camera-to-scale angle and pose.
6. Rectify the image or directly transform detected image coordinates into scale coordinates.
7. Report the angle-compensated measurement.

The key advantage is that angle estimation is based not only on mark locations but also on the expected color appearance of the known pattern. This allows the system to distinguish true scale position from apparent shifts or color changes caused by camera tilt, improving accuracy when the camera cannot remain perfectly perpendicular to the scale.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract for a reference scale and dimensional measurement apparatus in which a patterned film and lens produce a detectable length reference under varying viewing angles, without requiring the scale to be projected onto the object’s surface.
counterfactuals.output: A reference scale and dimensional measurement apparatus includes a patterned film having a plurality of scale indicia and an optical element disposed in a predetermined relationship with the patterned film. The optical element may comprise a lenticular, cylindrical, or microlens array configured to optically combine, magnify, or selectively reveal portions of the indicia to produce a detectable length reference at a plurality of viewing angles. The apparent spacing or position of the length reference is calibrated according to the geometry of the patterned film and optical element and may be compared with features of an object by an observer or an imaging system. One or more processors may identify the length reference in acquired images and determine an object dimension based on the calibrated reference. The apparatus provides a visible or machine-detectable scale without projecting the scale onto the object’s surface, thereby enabling dimensional measurements where surface projection is impractical or sensitive to surface texture, reflectivity, color, or orientation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
